_note: M9 pre-registration. Every constant a rule reads lives here and nowhere else (m8/CODEMAP.md pitfall 12: never mirror a registry constant into code). m9/LEDGER.md is the prose; this is the machine copy.

data.fineweb: EXCLUDED — no persisted reserved-set document fingerprints exist (m9/LEDGER.md 1.3)
data.doc_candidates_order: RNG draw order, NOT sorted (a sorted prefix is store-biased)

dose.precision: bf16 autocast backbone, loss in fp32

mix_arm.design: fixed-compute: identical optimizer updates AND identical non-pad tokens, split 70/30 BY TOKEN
mix_arm.batching: token-budgeted with a CUMULATIVE budget: each role fills until its running total reaches its share of the tokens due by the end of that step, so per-step rounding cannot accumulate. Streams are consumed in order and asserted never to run dry; every step is asserted non-empty.
mix_arm.loss_weighting: plain mean over all examples in the batch; no role weighting
mix_arm.challenger_branch: a selected challenger re-encodes the SAME 111,906 raw documents in its own space

dose.partial_batch: the final batch is trained at its natural size (32 examples)
dose.epoch_order: one default_rng(seed); fresh permutation(n) per epoch, concatenated
dose.retrieval_dtype: fp32 matmul from fp16 document memmaps

checkpoint_surfaces.SCREEN3: all four checkpoints -- 0.65 GB of document vectors, so it is nearly free and it carries the dose-response curve
checkpoint_surfaces.DEV6: the FINAL checkpoint only. A DEV-6 pass streams 23.3 GB of document vectors and, interleaved with training, fragments the allocator badly enough to cost more wall-clock than the training it measures. Reading it once, at the end, removes the interleaving
checkpoint_surfaces.consequence: the adequacy gate and the rank-stability rule both read SCREEN-3, which has all four points; the DECISION contrasts read DEV-6 at the final checkpoint, which is where they were always defined

dose.batch_size_note: locked at 128. The batch-32 pilot was registered and then REMOVED before any arm ran: two matched epochs give batch 32 four times the optimizer updates and compress a separate warmup+cosine schedule into a miniature, so it measures early optimization speed, not the batch size that wins at final dose (Codex pass 2, MAJOR-7). LEAF's bs=32 finding was made at roughly a hundred times this dose.

arm5_token_matched.why: prompt policy (a) prepends ~20 tokens per query; 16 full epochs would be a larger non-pad dose than the baseline and would confound prompt with dose

dose.token_budget_note: the batcher tracks T_base cumulatively; there is no per-step budget constant to go stale

teacher_swap.voids_downstream: a challenger win voids every student/prompt/mix decision taken under the incumbent and returns the milestone to Dylan; it never silently re-bases them
teacher_swap.status: NOT EXERCISED in M9. stella-400M stands as the teacher by default and by the owner's product preference -- one document model and one collection shared by zero and nano -- with a diagnostic measurement pointing the same way. The rule itself is unchanged and available.

rules.rank_stability_rule: a PROXY VETO, not a stability test of the decision surface: adoption is decided on DEV-6 at the final checkpoint while stability is measured on SCREEN-3, the only surface with four points (Codex pass 4). The contrast must have the same sign at the last two SCREEN-3 checkpoints; a flip means 'not stable at screen dose' -> default, arm recorded diagnostic.
rules.scope: every screen verdict is artifact-specific at the screen dose; never 'resolved', 'confirmed' or 'significant'

warm_start.what: the head is initialized to the closed-form ridge solution from the FROZEN backbone's mean-pooled outputs to the teacher targets, then trained normally with the rest of the model
warm_start.lambda_selected_on: a TRAINING-ONLY holdout: fit on the first 50,000 of the 60,000-text warm-start sample, score the remaining 10,000 under the ACTUAL normalized objective ||normalize(XA)-Y||^2, locked grid 1e-6..1, ties to the larger lambda. m9src/warmfit.py; the result is results/m9_warmfit.json and nano.warm_start_head refuses to run without it
warm_start.applies_to: every arm except the registered diagnostic contrast m9s1c
warm_start.evidence: results/m9_head_probe.json -- 0.3463 SCREEN-3 macro from a frozen backbone, 50.8% of the 0.6822 ceiling, against 12.4% for a random head after 2,000 trained steps
warm_start.withdrawn: the v3 claim that lambda was selected on the training residual. The head probe in fact selected argmax SCREEN-3, a dev surface (Codex pass 3, BLOCKER-B1). A residual criterion would not have rescued it: a ridge residual is monotone in lambda
warm_start.estimand: per-arm training-only-calibrated ridge initialization PLUS SGD. Each arm fits its own head in its own feature space under its own teacher's targets, so a contrast is end-to-end (factor + refit), not a pure factor contrast. Stated, not assumed away
warm_start.stage0_dose: 60,000 supervised backbone forwards + a 385x385 solve, reported separately from the SGD dose; the retention curve is read against both the SGD budget and total compute

A.purpose: the corrected, fully guarded anchor curve plus the M9.1 pilots. m9s1c prices the head warm start. m9s1c/m9s1b withdrawn 2026-08-30 (see their arm entries).

B.purpose: the three contrast arms that set the build's recipe: student, prompt, mix
B.order_amendment: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-30. The reorder (student/prompt/mix before the teacher arms) was justified by a time budget that no longer exists, and Codex pass 4 was right that the 'void later' rule is not equivalent to teacher-first: teacher-first PREVENTS invalid downstream experiments, while void-later runs them, inspects them and promises to discard them. Order restored to the mandate's. The void rule is kept as a belt-and-braces backstop, not as a justification.

diagnostics.note: run after the screen; decision-ineligible by construction (-diag id)

retention_at_final.why: below this the student sits so far from the teacher surface that a contrast between two arms is dominated by early-imitability rather than by the factor under test (Codex pass 2, MAJOR-9)

late_slope.why: a curve still climbing steeply at the final checkpoint is an early-training snapshot, and its ranking need not survive to final dose

outcomes.fail: stage B does NOT run. M9.1 reports the anchor curve, the warm-start contrast and a priced dose-response extrapolation, and the teacher/student/prompt/mix questions go back to Dylan with a budget attached rather than being answered at an inadequate dose

adequacy_gate.kind: a BUDGET TRIGGER, not a calibrated ranking-adequacy test. Neither threshold is tied to a measured rank-concordance rate, and the slope is a two-point difference read where the cosine schedule has already decayed the LR to 1e-5 -- so a small late gain can mean the schedule shut learning down rather than that the representation converged (Codex pass 3). It is used only to decide whether spending stage B is worth it; it certifies nothing
adequacy_gate.ceiling_from: registry ceilings.stella-400M-v5.SCREEN3, with the artifact hash pinned
